paras: The lynching of Dave Ramsey was the killing of a Black man by a mob at or near Marianna, Lee County, Arkansas, in January 1881, after he was accused of assaulting the young daughter of C. H. Banks, a local official called the sheriff in some reports. Accounts agree that he was riddled with bullets without trial but differ on whether he was taken from the jail or caught in a pursuit, and on whether he was also hanged. The story ran as a short wire item in papers from Georgia to Minnesota, several of which headlined it as just or speedy punishment.

According to a Little Rock dispatch, a daughter of C. H. Banks of Marianna was "brutally outraged by a colored man", who was then arrested and jailed. The Little Rock Democrat, reprinted in Memphis, gave a different account: Dave Ramsey met the twelve-year-old daughter of "one of the county officials" on the edge of town and attempted to assault her, but her cries frightened him away. The papers dated the alleged assault variously to Saturday, January 8, Tuesday, January 11, or January 12.

In the wire version, "an infuriated mob" surrounded the jail, forced the doors, took the prisoner a short distance from town and riddled his body with bullets. A variant of the same dispatch said the mob "overpowered the guards", and a Minnesota brief dated the seizure from the jail to January 11.

The Little Rock Democrat mentioned no jail; it said the girl's father told his friends, "the whole town turned out in pursuit", and Ramsey was quickly captured, hanged to the nearest tree and shot. Another brief described an "armed mob" divided between those who wanted to hang him and those who shot him "before the hanging faction could reach a tree". The Batesville Guard, an Arkansas weekly, said only that he was "shot to death by a body of citizens near Marianna".
No report of an inquest, arrests or any official response appears in the coverage.

The story reached most papers through a New Orleans telegram of January 13 quoting a Little Rock dispatch, printed on January 14 in Savannah and Richmond and a week later in South Carolina. Southern headlines approved of the killing: the Savannah Morning News called it "A Brutal Outrage and Its Speedy Punishment", the Union Times "A Negro Ravisher Riddled with Bullets", and the Memphis Public Ledger "Just Punishment". The Memphis paper's reprint of the Little Rock Democrat called the accused "the fiend" and "the brute" and was the only account to name him.

Northern weeklies in Pennsylvania, Ohio and Minnesota carried the item in news summaries between January 19 and 21, often in a single sentence. Their wording repeated the wire's assumptions, with the Somerset Herald calling the prisoner "the darkey" and the Worthington Advance "the villain". The Raleigh Farmer and Mechanic reduced it to one line, that a Black man "was lynched at Marianna, Ark., for rape."

The main dispute is over custody and method: the wire and several briefs describe a jail seizure and shooting, while the Little Rock Democrat describes a pursuit, a hanging and a shooting with no jail. The wire said the girl was "brutally outraged", whereas the Democrat said the attacker was frightened away before completing the assault; both were accusations that never came before a court. The father's name also appears as "Bank" and "Bonds" in some printings of the wire.

reader.title: Lynching of Dave Ramsey
bases: Every account says a mob or 'body of citizens' killed a Black man accused of assaulting a girl at Marianna, Arkansas, without trial (A1, A3, A6).

A mob, 'the whole town' or 'a body of citizens' shot (and in one version hanged) the accused man without legal process (A1, A3, A6); the papers present the killing as punishment for an alleged assault on a white girl (A3, A9).

The New Orleans wire (A1), the Little Rock Democrat as reprinted in Memphis (A3) and the Batesville Guard (A6) agree that a Black man accused of assaulting the Banks girl was killed by a mob near Marianna, though they differ on the date, the jail and the method; the wire and A3 may both go back to Little Rock reports.

accounts.label: Wire report (Little Rock dispatch via New Orleans)
accounts.gist: The man was arrested and jailed after a 'brutal' outrage; a mob surrounded the jail, forced the doors (or overpowered the guards), took him a short distance from town and riddled his body with bullets.

accounts.label: Little Rock Democrat
accounts.gist: Dave Ramsey attempted to assault a 12-year-old girl on Saturday and was frightened away; the whole town pursued him, and he was captured, hanged to the nearest tree and his body riddled. No jail is mentioned.

accounts.label: Batesville Guard (Arkansas)
accounts.gist: A Black man was shot to death by 'a body of citizens near Marianna' for an assault on Sheriff Banks's daughter.

accounts.label: Worthington advance
accounts.gist: An armed mob took him from jail, and some members shot him before 'the hanging faction' could reach a tree.

framing.detail: The Memphis Public Ledger headed the Little Rock Democrat's account 'Just Punishment' and 'A Brutal Negro Lynched', calling the man 'the fiend' and 'the brute'.
The Savannah Morning News headed the wire 'A Brutal Outrage and Its Speedy Punishment'; the Union Times headed it 'A Negro Ravisher Riddled with Bullets'.
Northern and Midwestern papers ran short items in news columns, some still calling him 'the darkey', 'a negro ravisher' or 'the villain'.

record_check.dossier: Jan. 12 is the wire's date for the alleged assault, not clearly the killing; other versions give Jan. 11 or Jan. 8 for the assault, and one dates the jail seizure to the 11th. Best stated as Jan. 8-12, 1881.

Marianna, Lee County, Arkansas; killed 'a short distance from town' (wire) or 'near Marianna'.
One Black man, named as Dave Ramsey only in the Little Rock Democrat; other papers call him 'a colored man' or 'a negro'.
Accused of 'brutally' outraging the daughter of C. H. Banks (wire), or of attempting to assault a 12-year-old daughter of a county official and being frightened away (Little Rock Democrat).
'An infuriated mob' (wire); 'the whole town' (Little Rock Democrat); 'a body of citizens' (Batesville Guard); 'an armed mob' with a 'hanging faction' (Worthington advance).
